web/_aws_ecs_acceptance/secure_documents:
R6 `except InterruptedError: continue` in `_flock_retry_interrupted`. The value is the kernel's EINTR result from `_fcntl.flock(descriptor, operation)` on the receipt-manifest sidecar lock: a signal delivered to the acceptance process, not this code, decides whether the call returns, so it is Tier-3 in the only sense that matters here — unowned and non-deterministic. Nothing is defaulted, skipped, or fabricated: the handler's sole action is to re-issue the identical flock call, which is the PEP 475 contract Python applies to the syscalls it wraps and the only correct response to an interrupted lock acquisition. Returning from `_receipt_manifest_write_lock` without the lock would let two acceptance processes run a read-modify-write on the same manifest, which is exactly the race `_serialized_control_manifest_write` and `receipt_store` exist to prevent.

CONTROL, BY SYMBOL. The only caller, `_receipt_manifest_write_lock` (verified with `git grep -n _flock_retry_interrupted`), wraps each call in `except OSError: raise AcceptanceCheckError(check) from None` — for LOCK_EX and again for LOCK_UN in its `finally` — so every non-EINTR failure (EBADF, ENOLCK, EWOULDBLOCK) escapes as a fail-closed check failure. The retry loop absorbs exactly one errno and nothing else. It is unbounded by design: EINTR is transient by definition, and a bounded retry that gave up would have to either return unlocked (unsafe) or raise on a transient (a spurious acceptance failure that an operator would then re-run without any defect having existed).

PINNED by `tests/unit/web/aws_ecs_acceptance/test_contracts_secure_state.py::test_receipt_manifest_lock_retries_interrupted_flock`, which injects one InterruptedError on the first LOCK_EX and asserts the exact operation sequence `[LOCK_EX, LOCK_EX, LOCK_UN]` — one interruption, one re-issue, no double-lock, no skipped unlock.

WHY NOT RESTRUCTURE. The only shapes that clear R6 are a re-raise or a non-default return inside the handler; either would turn a retry into a failure or a silent unlocked return. Shaping the loop around the rule would degrade the mechanism it protects.
web/_aws_ecs_acceptance/textract.py:R4:v:
R4 `except Exception: close_failed = True` inside the `finally` of `verify_textract`, around `client.close()`. The value is Tier-3: whatever the boto3 Textract client's `close()` raises during urllib3 pool / socket teardown. The handler cannot re-raise: it runs inside a `finally`, and a raise there REPLACES any in-flight exception from the probe body, so a `textract_resource_close` error would mask the primary `AcceptanceCheckError` (`textract_start_document_analysis`, `textract_get_document_analysis`, `textract_profile_*`) that names the action that actually failed — the signal an operator acts on.

CONTROL, BY SYMBOL. The flag is consumed on the very next statement after the `finally`: `if close_failed: raise AcceptanceCheckError("textract_resource_close")`. Nothing is swallowed: when the probes succeed, a close failure still fails the check, so a leaked SDK client can never produce a passing verify-textract receipt; when a probe fails, the probe's own error wins and the close failure is subordinate. R4 fires purely because `TierModelVisitor._check_exception_handler` requires an `ast.Raise` inside the handler body; it never consults the statement that consumes the flag.

WHY BROAD. The exception classes reachable through botocore/urllib3 teardown are not enumerable by this module, and narrowing to a tuple would trade R4 for R6 at the same site with no behaviour gain. The raw exception text is never carried into the error — `AcceptanceCheckError` names only the static check id — matching the sanitisation contract every other probe site in this module follows.

PINNED by `tests/unit/web/aws_ecs_acceptance/test_textract.py::test_verify_textract_reports_close_failure_after_successful_probes` (close failure after successful probes → `textract_resource_close`) and `tests/unit/web/aws_ecs_acceptance/test_textract.py::test_verify_textract_probe_failure_wins_over_close_failure` (probe failure plus close failure → the probe's check id, and `client.closed is True`, so close still ran).
